post.caption: Intaglio gems can hide a battle scene. An intaglio is a design cut down into a stone. Press it into wax or clay and the image stands up. The word is Italian, from intagliare, meaning to cut in. Cylinder seals rolled across wet clay appeared over 5,000 years ago. Carvers turned drills with a bow and cut with emery powder. Signet gems pressed into wax marked ownership and sealed letters. The engraver Dioscurides signed an amethyst portrait of Demosthenes. The Pylos Combat Agate is about 3,500 years old. Its battle scene shows clearly only under magnification.
